result.title: HypoLoop: Revising Weight-Editing Plans from Scientific Feedback
result.summary: Scientific experiments continually reveal prediction errors. Effective updates depend on which parameters change and which errors drive the correction. We introduce HypoLoop, a family of native weight-editing methods that connects these choices to experimental feedback. Fixed, numerically adaptive, and LLM-guided policies produce editing plans; numerical solvers compute weight patches, and internal validation selects the deployed predictor. Successive observations and validation records support revisions to editable locations and fitting rules. Experiments cover 22 scientific tasks and both DeepSeek and Claude. On Burgers, reallocating a matched parameter budget reduces error by 58.80% and 47.72% relative to fixed locations. On DIODE, positive-residual weighting reduces absolute relative error (AbsRel) by 13.35% in internal cross-validation, with the same 33 editable coordinates. Revising the complete plan across rounds lowers final AbsRel by 10.59% relative to keeping the initial plan fixed. SpaceNet7 and Make3D connect accepted edits to improved spatial predictions. These results show how experimental evidence can shape the update problem itself. Code: https://github.com/limengran98/HypoLoop.

AI.brief_summary: HypoLoop 提出一组面向科学预测的权重编辑方法：由固定、数值自适应或 LLM 引导策略生成编辑计划，数值求解器计算权重补丁，并用内部验证选择部署的预测器，在 22 个科学任务上比较不同参数分配与计划修订带来的误差变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「依观测与验证记录决定改哪些参数、由哪类残差误差驱动修正」的反馈式计划修订，可能为 LVR 中该更新哪些内部状态与贡献分配提供核查线索，但该文不涉及视觉语言推理，迁移需较多判断。
